title: Beef, steak, sirloin, lean and fat

content.title: About
content.content: Sirloin steak is a cut taken from the lumbar region of a cow. Depending on the amount of intramuscular fat it can be lean (under 5 % fat) or moderately fatty (up to 15 % fat). The steak is usually grilled, pan‑seared or roasted, preserving its juiciness and characteristic beef flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sirloin is considered one of the most tender beef cuts.
Lean steaks are popular in diet plans, while fattier ones are prized for richer taste.
Beef provides all essential amino acids required by humans.
Traditionally the steak is cooked to medium doneness to keep it juicy.
In the US it is called “sirloin steak”, in Russia – “стейк из вырезки”.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef steak supplies complete protein needed for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is more readily absorbed than plant iron, helping prevent anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals aid immune response and protect against oxidative stress.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Creatine in meat can improve strength and endurance during physical activity.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Fattier cuts may raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli.

items.title: Allergy or sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels can exacerbate gout symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steak is typically cooked to the desired doneness (rare, medium‑rare, medium, well‑done). It can be served with vegetables, potatoes, sauces, or simply seasoned with salt and pepper. Lean cuts benefit from a quick sear over high heat, while fattier pieces are better cooked more slowly to melt the fat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2‑3 days. For longer storage freeze it in an airtight bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 6‑12 months. Thaw frozen steak in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
